root.name: Benoni Defense: King's Pawn Line
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 e6 4. Nc3 exd5 5. cxd5 d6 6. e4

overview: This is the Modern Benoni main structure: White has a space-gaining pawn centre on d5/e4 and a kingside majority, Black has a queenside majority, the half-open e- and b-files and the long diagonal for the g7 bishop. After 6...g6 White chooses between the Classical (Nf3, Be2), the Fianchetto and sharper tries such as f4 and Bb5+. White aims for e5 and a kingside push, Black for ...b5 and play against the e4 pawn, and both sides know the lines well. The play is double-edged and theory-heavy.

white_ideas.idea: Break with e5 or f4 and attack in the centre and on the kingside
Develop Nf3, Be2, O-O and Nd2 to hold e4
Use the space advantage and keep the d5 pawn supported

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto with ...g6 and ...Bg7, castle and play ...Re8
Break on the queenside with ...b5 and ...a6, using the half-open b-file
Pressure e4 and place a knight on e5 or c5 as an outpost

typical_structures.structure: Modern Benoni: White d5/e4 against Black c5/d6, a locked-ish centre with the e-file and b-file half open

character.notes: Both sides take risks: White attacks the king with f4, e5 or Bb5+, Black counterattacks on the queenside; one slip loses fast.

gambit.notes: The c5 pawn is exchanged on d5, no pawn is offered (the Benko is a different line).

soundness.notes: Sound; Black's structure is dynamic but accepted at top level.

structure.notes: White d5 and e4 against c5 and d6 gives a fixed asymmetric centre, with half-open e- and b-files rather than a fully locked chain.

approach.notes: A mainline-style defence with its own theory; not a universal set-up.

level.notes: Black must know the White attacks in detail (Taimanov Attack, Bb5+) and also understand the plans.

sublines_that_differ.name: Taimanov Attack
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 e6 4. Nc3 exd5 5. cxd5 d6 6. e4 g6 7. f4 Bg7 8. Bb5+
sublines_that_differ.how: A more forcing attack that Black must meet accurately.

sublines_that_differ.name: Be7 Classical
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 e6 4. Nc3 exd5 5. cxd5 d6 6. e4 Be7
sublines_that_differ.how: Less common; Black keeps the bishop for a different set-up.

character.reason: Opposite plans on the wings and a risk of fast tactics.

structure.reason: A fixed asymmetric centre with half-open e- and b-files; Closed is the alternative.

approach.reason: A recognised main-line defence rather than a universal set-up.

level.reason: Heavy theory in the attacking lines and hard plans for Black.

plans.reason: White's space and centre against Black's queenside majority.
